Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## gh-829 — CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation

### Root Cause
`validate-fresh-masked-green` (gh-759) matches green zero-label heads only when mergeState is BLOCKED — CLEAN was excluded ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"). But `merge-validated` requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated, so a fresh machine PR that is CLEAN + green + zero labels matched no rule and rotted (live: PR #826, hours idle).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — new query guard `mergeStateLatch`: a listed merge state matches ONLY when the PR's linked issue carries the latch label(s), read via the existing per-tick TTL issue-label cache; fails CLOSED (no linked issue / fetch failure / missing label ⇒ state excluded, exactly like the old `notMergeState`).
- `sm_github.json` — `validate-fresh-masked-green`: `notMergeState` drops CLEAN (now `[BEHIND, DIRTY]`), adds `"mergeStateLatch": {"CLEAN": ["ai_developed"]}`. CLEAN + green + zero lifecycle labels + the issue's `ai_developed` latch (AC1) flows through the unchanged `validate_pr` probe → dispatch + arm; `skipIfGreenCi` stays. The BLOCKED branch is untouched — still author-agnostic, no latch, no issue fetch (gh-757 contract).
- AC2: all five lifecycle labels stay in `notLabels` — every existing rule keeps its lane. AC3: guest/unlinked PRs without the latch stay unarmed (fail closed).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: new `gh-829` suite in `test_smGithubSource.js` fails on the pre-fix engine (CLEAN heads arm indiscriminately; pr-826 invisible to every arming rule).
- Matrix L1: labels × mergeState × latch — 15-PR wave pinning AC1/AC2/AC3, fail-closed fetch, unlinked PR, BLOCKED-branch parity, drafts, checks-none lane.
- `test_smAgent.js` config assertions updated to the deployed rule shape.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2253 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- L2 (replay of #826's 5h timeline) and L3 (live) verify in deployment; the unit wave reproduces the exact #826 shape (green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` latch).
- No new API pressure: the latch reuses the 60s issue-label cache already maintained for priority tiers.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

## References

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

- No new API pressure: the latch reuses the 60s issue-label cache already maintained for priority tiers.

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

Is that a problem? notMergeState guard above already excludes when `!item.pr`. But if a rule has ONLY mergeStateLatch without notMergeState, an item without `pr` would pass. 3. More important: **BLOCKED + latch semantics**. The latch map is `{ CLEAN: ['ai_developed'] }`. But the guard: if `latchState` is BLOCKED, `latchWant = q.mergeStateLatch['BLOCKED']` = undefined → skip guard → matches. So BLOCKED branch is untouched. Good.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## PR Description

Closes #829
## gh-829 — CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation

### Root Cause
`validate-fresh-masked-green` (gh-759) matches green zero-label heads only when mergeState is BLOCKED — CLEAN was excluded ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"). But `merge-validated` requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated, so a fresh machine PR that is CLEAN + green + zero labels matched no rule and rotted (live: PR #826, hours idle).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — new query guard `mergeStateLatch`: a listed merge state matches ONLY when the PR's linked issue carries the latch label(s), read via the existing per-tick TTL issue-label cache; fails CLOSED (no linked issue / fetch failure / missing label ⇒ state excluded, exactly like the old `notMergeState`).
- `sm_github.json` — `validate-fresh-masked-green`: `notMergeState` drops CLEAN (now `[BEHIND, DIRTY]`), adds `"mergeStateLatch": {"CLEAN": ["ai_developed"]}`. CLEAN + green + zero lifecycle labels + the issue's `ai_developed` latch (AC1) flows through the unchanged `validate_pr` probe → dispatch + arm; `skipIfGreenCi` stays. The BLOCKED branch is untouched — still author-agnostic, no latch, no issue fetch (gh-757 contract).
- AC2: all five lifecycle labels stay in `notLabels` — every existing rule keeps its lane. AC3: guest/unlinked PRs without the latch stay unarmed (fail closed).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: new `gh-829` suite in `test_smGithubSource.js` fails on the pre-fix engine (CLEAN heads arm indiscriminately; pr-826 invisible to every arming rule).
- Matrix L1: labels × mergeState × latch — 15-PR wave pinning AC1/AC2/AC3, fail-closed fetch, unlinked PR, BLOCKED-branch parity, drafts, checks-none lane.
- `test_smAgent.js` config assertions updated to the deployed rule shape.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2253 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- L2 (replay of #826's 5h timeline) and L3 (live) verify in deployment; the unit wave reproduces the exact #826 shape (green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` latch).
- No new API pressure: the latch reuses the 60s issue-label cache already maintained for priority tiers.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

## PR Description

## gh-829 — CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation

### Root Cause
`validate-fresh-masked-green` (gh-759) matches green zero-label heads only when mergeState is BLOCKED — CLEAN was excluded ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"). But `merge-validated` requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated, so a fresh machine PR that is CLEAN + green + zero labels matched no rule and rotted (live: PR #826, hours idle).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — new query guard `mergeStateLatch`: a listed merge state matches ONLY when the PR's linked issue carries the latch label(s), read via the existing per-tick TTL issue-label cache; fails CLOSED (no linked issue / fetch failure / missing label ⇒ state excluded, exactly like the old `notMergeState`).
- `sm_github.json` — `validate-fresh-masked-green`: `notMergeState` drops CLEAN (now `[BEHIND, DIRTY]`), adds `"mergeStateLatch": {"CLEAN": ["ai_developed"]}`. CLEAN + green + zero lifecycle labels + the issue's `ai_developed` latch (AC1) flows through the unchanged `validate_pr` probe → dispatch + arm; `skipIfGreenCi` stays. The BLOCKED branch is untouched — still author-agnostic, no latch, no issue fetch (gh-757 contract).
- AC2: all five lifecycle labels stay in `notLabels` — every existing rule keeps its lane. AC3: guest/unlinked PRs without the latch stay unarmed (fail closed).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: new `gh-829` suite in `test_smGithubSource.js` fails on the pre-fix engine (CLEAN heads arm indiscriminately; pr-826 invisible to every arming rule).
- Matrix L1: labels × mergeState × latch — 15-PR wave pinning AC1/AC2/AC3, fail-closed fetch, unlinked PR, BLOCKED-branch parity, drafts, checks-none lane.
- `test_smAgent.js` config assertions updated to the deployed rule shape.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2253 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- L2 (replay of #826's 5h timeline) and L3 (live) verify in deployment; the unit wave reproduces the exact #826 shape (green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` latch).
- No new API pressure: the latch reuses the 60s issue-label cache already maintained for priority tiers.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

## References

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). # gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

## References

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

Is that a problem? notMergeState guard above already excludes when `!item.pr`. But if a rule has ONLY mergeStateLatch without notMergeState, an item without `pr` would pass. Closes #829
## gh-829 — CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation

### Root Cause
`validate-fresh-masked-green` (gh-759) matches green zero-label heads only when mergeState is BLOCKED — CLEAN was excluded ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"). But `merge-validated` requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated, so a fresh machine PR that is CLEAN + green + zero labels matched no rule and rotted (live: PR #826, hours idle).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — new query guard `mergeStateLatch`: a listed merge state matches ONLY when the PR's linked issue carries the latch label(s), read via the existing per-tick TTL issue-label cache; fails CLOSED (no linked issue / fetch failure / missing label ⇒ state excluded, exactly like the old `notMergeState`).
- `sm_github.json` — `validate-fresh-masked-green`: `notMergeState` drops CLEAN (now `[BEHIND, DIRTY]`), adds `"mergeStateLatch": {"CLEAN": ["ai_developed"]}`. CLEAN + green + zero lifecycle labels + the issue's `ai_developed` latch (AC1) flows through the unchanged `validate_pr` probe → dispatch + arm; `skipIfGreenCi` stays. The BLOCKED branch is untouched — still author-agnostic, no latch, no issue fetch (gh-757 contract).
- AC2: all five lifecycle labels stay in `notLabels` — every existing rule keeps its lane. AC3: guest/unlinked PRs without the latch stay unarmed (fail closed).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: new `gh-829` suite in `test_smGithubSource.js` fails on the pre-fix engine (CLEAN heads arm indiscriminately; pr-826 invisible to every arming rule).
- Matrix L1: labels × mergeState × latch — 15-PR wave pinning AC1/AC2/AC3, fail-closed fetch, unlinked PR, BLOCKED-branch parity, drafts, checks-none lane.
- `test_smAgent.js` config assertions updated to the deployed rule shape.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2253 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- L2 (replay of #826's 5h timeline) and L3 (live) verify in deployment; the unit wave reproduces the exact #826 shape (green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` latch).
- No new API pressure: the latch reuses the 60s issue-label cache already maintained for priority tiers.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

## References

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.

# gh-829: [GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)

## Description

## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park.     "summary": "[GOAL] CLEAN + green + ZERO-labels machine PR never arms validation — dead-zone family misses the CLEAN case (dmtools-agents PR #826 sat idle)",
    "description": "## Goal

A freshly-created machine PR whose head is CLEAN with GREEN checks and ZERO labels must get validation armed in the same tick — the gh-757/759 dead-zone family only covers BLOCKED heads, so CLEAN+green+no-labels PRs are never armed and rot.

## Subject

Tick arming rules: `validate-fresh` (checks none/pending) and the gh-759 `validate-unarmed-green` (green + BLOCKED). Both exclude CLEAN — deliberately ("merge-validated owns CLEAN"), but merge-validated requires `pr_approved`, which a zero-label PR can never reach without first being validated. The exclusion assumed SOME rule covers the CLEAN+no-labels case; none does.

Live instance 2026-10-10: dmtools-agents PR #826 (issue gh-825 latch `ai_developed` present, PR all-green, CLEAN, zero labels for hours — no `ai_validating`, no review, nothing; owner flagged it as "не двигается").

## Capability surface

- Extend `validate-unarmed-green` (gh-759): drop the CLEAN exclusion for the ZERO-LABEL case only — green + not-BEHIND + none of `ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed` + PR's issue carries `ai_developed` ⇒ probe for a dispatched CI run (existing logic) ⇒ dispatch + arm.
- KEEP the notMergeState exclusions for BEHIND/DIRTY as today (silent-update/conflict paths own those).
- The `skipIfGreenCi` guard stays (green completed run covers head ⇒ skip, log why).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — fresh machine PR, green ambient checks, CLEAN, zero labels, `ai_developed` issue latch ⇒ one tick arms `ai_validating` + dispatches validation.
2. AC2: a PR with ANY lifecycle label is untouched by this rule (all existing rules keep their disjointness).
3. AC3: guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today).
4. AC4: live — #826-class occurrence arms within one tick, no manual intervention.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (match/no-match matrix over labels × mergeState × latch).
- L2: replay #826's timeline (green+CLEAN+zero labels ~5h) — new rule arms at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next fresh dev PR arms promptly.

## Non-goals

- Changing kicker/ambient-check behavior.
- The thread-resolution card (#828) — independent.

## References

- gh-756/#757/#759 dead-zone family (fa #1305-#1312, #922 instances).
- Instance: dmtools-agents PR #826, 2026-10-10.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38030008514) · started 06:10 · done 06:24 ✅"

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

blocks.text:
Key observations:

1. `cachedIssueLabels` on fetch failure returns `null` — good, fail-closed semantics apply to the latch: `if (!latchIssue) return false`. But wait — an important nuance: if labels fetched successfully but the issue has zero labels, `issueLabels(obj)` — what does it return? Probably `[]`. Then `latchIssue = []` which is truthy in JS! `![]` is false, so we don't return false at the null check; then the loop `latchIssue.indexOf(latchWant[li]) === -1` → return false. Good — missing label excludes. Correct fail-closed.

2. Bug check: the latch guard placement. `if (latchWant) { ... }` — if `q.mergeStateLatch` exists but the current mergeState is NOT listed (e.g. BLOCKED), `latchWant` is null and we proceed — fine, matches the BLOCKED branch. But wait — there's a subtle issue: what if mergeState IS listed but `item.pr` is null? `latchState = null`, `latchWant = null`, proceed → the item matches. Is that a problem? notMergeState guard above already excludes when `!item.pr`. But if a rule has ONLY mergeStateLatch without notMergeState, an item without `pr` would pass. In the configured rule, notMergeState covers BEHIND/DIRTY, but an item with no `pr`... queryPrs items — do they always have pr? Let me check. Actually `nmsWant && (!item.pr || ...)` returns false when item.pr missing — so in the deployed rule, items without pr are excluded. Fine.

3. More important: **BLOCKED + latch semantics**. The latch map is `{ CLEAN: ['ai_developed'] }`. But the guard: if `latchState` is BLOCKED, `latchWant = q.mergeStateLatch['BLOCKED']` = undefined → skip guard → matches. So BLOCKED branch is untouched. Good.

4. What if mergeState is CLEAN and latch present — item passes only when issue labels contain ai_developed. But wait — the guard checks `item.issueNumber`. Where does `issueNumber` come from on PR items? Let me verify PR items get issueNumber populated. If item.issueNumber is missing, latchIssue is null → return false → fail closed. Good for safety but does it make AC1 unachievable if PRs don't carry issueNumber? Need to check how PR items are enriched.

5. **Race/caching with stale `null`**: fetch failure cached as `null` for 60s — a transient failure excludes the state for up to 60s, not forever. Acceptable.

6. **The cache comment says "PR-side labels only, tier degrades toward medium"** — fine.

7. Check ordering: latch guard runs AFTER notMergeState. Fine.

8. Potential issue: `q.mergeStateLatch` iterating — what if `latchWant` is not an array but a string? Config uses array. Minor robustness; notMergeState handles both forms (Array.isArray check). The latch doesn't handle string form. Suggestion-level.

9. Another subtle thing: the latch guard is inside `matchesGuards`, which is called from `queryIssues` too. In queryIssues, do items have `pr`? Yes, enriched items presumably. Passing repoInfo is fine.

10. Check `cachedIssueLabels` visibility: defined above matchesGuards at module scope — fine, function declaration hoisted anyway.

11. **Double negative concern**: `if (q.mergeStateLatch)` block — if the state is listed AND all labels present, the loop completes and we fall through. Correct.

12. Now, `notLabels` includes 'validation_failed' — per verdict rules label guardrails, fine.

Now check where issueNumber comes from for PR items, and check test files. Let me read the rest of githubSource.js relevant parts and the tests.

blocks.text:
Wait — there's a subtle bug in the test harness's mergedTools in the new gh-829 suite: `load(tools, prs, statuses, issueLabels, issueErrors)` — in the "BLOCKED branch needs no latch" test, they call `load({github_list_prs...}, {}, {...})` — without issueLabels/issueErrors, so the default `github_get_issue` resolves labels as `[]`. Fine.

But important: `Object.keys(tools || {}).forEach(function (k) { mergedTools[k] = tools[k]; })` — tools with github_list_prs override only. Good.

Note the mock `github_get_issue` in the new suite returns `{ number: n, labels: ls.map(...) }` — objects with `name`. And `issueLabels(obj)` in githubSource — let me check how it extracts labels. If `obj.labels` is array of `{name: ...}`, `issueLabels` presumably maps. Check.

Also check `parseMcp`. Not critical.

Now — check `queryPrs`: how mergeState flows. Statuses: `prStatus` returns `{state, checks, mergeState, mergeable}`. In queryPrs, `item.pr` is set presumably from provider.prStatus. Let me verify `item.pr.mergeState` exists and `item.issueNumber` populated via `linkedIssueNumber(item.body)`.

Also check that the gh-759 suite's `load` change (default github_get_issue returning `{ number, labels: [] }`) — in that suite the OLD RULE still used? The gh-759 suite's RULE was updated to the new shape with latch, and issues resolve to label-less → CLEAN excluded. Fine.

One potential issue in the gh-759 suite update: the default stub `github_get_issue` returns `labels: []` (array of strings? No — `labels: []` empty, fine) — but what shape does `issueLabels(obj)` expect? Empty array is fine either way.

Now, deeper review questions:

1. **Interaction with priorityTier cache staleness for tests**: `_priorityIssueLabelCache` is module-level and persists across tests within the same loaded module. Since `load()` reloads the module each time (loadModule fresh), cache is fresh per test. OK.

2. **Potential correctness issue — latch with `item.pr` missing**: covered by notMergeState in deployed rule, but as a generic guard semantics, an item without `pr` whose mergeState lookup yields null skips the latch entirely and matches. If someone later adds mergeStateLatch without notMergeState, a pr-less item would pass. Minor defensive note; SUGGESTION.

3. **The `latchWant` string vs array**: config contract is arrays. If someone writes `"mergeStateLatch": {"CLEAN": "ai_developed"}`, then `latchWant.length` is string length and `indexOf` checks substring — `'ai_developed'.indexOf('ai_developed') === 0` works for single full-string... actually `'ai_developed'.indexOf('ai_developed')` = 0 ≠ -1, passes. For multi-char it might false-positive with substrings. But config is controlled. SUGGESTION at most. Actually the codebase pattern for notMergeState explicitly normalizes string→array. Could apply same. SUGGESTION.

4. **AC check**: AC1 sim — yes, new suite. AC2 — labels matrix tested. AC3 — guest stays unarmed via latch absence. But note AC3 says "guest-authored PRs without the latch stay unarmed (machine-author gating as today)". Hmm — the rule itself is author-agnostic (gh-757 contract: validation dispatch is not machine-gated, only auto-REWORK arm). For CLEAN, gating happens via the issue latch, not the author. A guest PR whose linked issue has ai_developed... could a guest PR link to a machine-developed issue? Edge case: issue gh-825 has ai_developed; a guest opens a PR "Closes #825" that's green + CLEAN + zero labels → validation would be armed for a guest PR. Previously (pre-gh-829), CLEAN excluded everyone, BLOCKED included everyone (deliberately). The latch gates on the issue, not authorship — matches the PR description's stated design ("machine-work gating, guests stay unarmed" — assuming guests don't latch onto machine issues). This is a design decision documented; not a blocker. Worth a note? The BLOCKED branch is deliberately author-agnostic per gh-757, so consistency argues the CLEAN latch-on-issue approach is fine. I might raise as SUGGESTION theoretical guest-PR-riding-a-machine-issue case, but it's quite marginal and the description explicitly discusses it. Maybe skip or suggestion.

5. **`checks` guard and skipIfGreenCi** unchanged.

6. **sm_github.json description update** — large doc string. Check the JSON is valid and the rule shape. Let me view the rule in sm_github.json.

7. **CI status**: no ci_failures.md input — so CI presumably green or unknown. The PR description says full suite 2253 passed. Let me run the unit tests? That could take a while, but we could run the two test files. Let's check test runner. `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` may not work locally. Let me see if there's a local runner, e.g. node. Check how tests run.

8. **Check `linkedIssueNumber`** — parses body for "Closes #N". PR-829 in the wave has body 'no anchor here' → unlinked → fail closed. Good.

9. One more: **cache poisoning across repos**: key includes owner/repo. Good.

10. **Cache `null` entry truthiness check**: `var hit = _priorityIssueLabelCache.entries[key]; if (hit) {...}` — entries are objects `{at, data}` — truthy even when data null. Fine.

11. **Latch evaluated before the stale-review guard** — order irrelevant.

12. Potential issue: `matchesGuards` is also used by `queryIssues`. In queryIssues, items are issues with `item.pr` possibly null; passing repoInfo — was repoInfo previously available in that scope? Yes, queryIssues has repoInfo param already (used at line 453 etc.). Fine.

13. **Description length in sm_github.json** — massively long description (already long before; PR adds another big paragraph). Maintainability nit — existing style though. SUGGESTION at most, probably skip since it matches existing pattern.

Let me check `issueLabels` helper and `linkedIssueNumber`, plus the sm_github.json rule, then run the tests.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI
